To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neutrophils cause relaxation of normotension rat aortas with or without endothelial cells and contraction of SHR aortas with endothelial cells.

the response of aortas from SHR to neutrophil factors depends on the presence of endothelium; the response of aorta from normotensive rat to neutrophil factor(s) depends on the presence or absence of endothelium.
neutrophils from hypertensive rats cause contraction of aorta from hypertensive rats, whereas neutrophils from normotensive cause relaxation of aorta from normotensive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of activated neutrophils in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
the effects of neutrophils on the aortic ring from spontaneously hypertensive rat.
the role of neutrophil activation products in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SHR neutrophils are not the culprit for the hypertension.
neutrophils from normotensive and hypertensive rats cause endothelium-independent relaxation of rat aorta by releasing nitric oxide.
SHR neutrophils, when activated, produce an agent that causes contraction of the aortic ring of normotensive rats but not SHR rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neutrophils from SHR and Wistar-Kyoto rats have a different response to aortic rings, and the difference in the response is not due to a difference in the production of superoxide anions.
neutrophils from spontaneously hypertensive rat (SHR) caused a cell number dependent relaxation followed by contraction in normotensive rat and SHR aorta.

neutrophil-derived superoxide anion is responsible for the contraction of hypertensive rat aorta and neutrophil-derived nitric oxide and prostaglandin I2 are responsible for relaxation in normotensive rat and hypertensive rat aortas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neutrophils obtained either from hypertensive or from normotensive rat strains can cause relaxation or contraction of rat aorta, depending on the presence of endothelium or not.
neutrophils obtained both from normotensive and hypertensive rats cause relaxation and contraction of aortic rings.
the endothelium of aortas from SHR is more sensitive than that from control rats to the contractile action of superoxide anions produced by neutrophils.
